issues.legal_issue: A proceeding to recover tax as arrears of land revenue commences when the assessing authority requests the Collector to recover the arrears, rather than when a later coercive recovery step is taken.
material_facts: The assessee defaulted in paying agricultural income tax and penalties assessed for several assessment years.
For several demands, the assessing authority directed the revenue officer to realise the amounts as arrears of land revenue within one year after the final instalment fell due.
For one demand, the direction to realise the amount was made more than one year after the final instalment fell due.
The attachment orders were issued after the one-year period had expired.
For another demand, the High Court accepted register entries as evidence that an order for realisation had been received within the one-year period, although the original order was missing.
issues.conclusion: The recovery proceedings commenced when the assessing authority made the request or order directing recovery as arrears of land revenue. Accordingly, recovery was not time-barred for demands for which that request was made within one year after the final instalment fell due, but was time-barred for the demand for which it was made later; the subsequent attachment date did not determine when proceedings commenced.
issues.legal_principle: Section 32(2) of the U.P. Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1949 bars commencement of recovery proceedings after one year from the date the final instalment falls due. Read with section 32(1), the provision means that proceedings commence when the assessing authority moves the Collector to recover the dues as arrears of land revenue, not when the Collector later takes an enforcement step. The Court held section 32 to be in pari materia with section 46 of the Income-tax Act, 1922, under which recovery proceedings commence when the Income-tax Officer forwards the recovery certificate to the Collector. The Court referred to the Allahabad High Court's decision in Lal Bhan Pratap Narain Bahadur Pal v. State of Uttar Pradesh and to the decisions discussed in Kishorilal v. Triloki Nath.

predicates.recovery_proceeding: A tax authority seeks to recover unpaid tax or related dues from a taxpayer as arrears of land revenue.
predicates.authority_request_within_limitation_peri: The assessing authority's request or order directing the Collector to recover the dues is made within the applicable limitation period measured from the final instalment's due date.

issues.definition: When a tax recovery proceeding involves a request by the assessing authority to the Collector within the applicable limitation period, the proceeding is not time-barred.
